name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its MoE design delivers 235B active parameters with 22B experts, hitting the sweet spot between raw power and efficiency—proven faster than DeepSeek-R1-671B on benchmarks while costing less per token. The trade-off is hardware dependency: it needs GPUs with 80GB+ VRAM, but that’s a one-time cost for a 0.5%+ lift in capability.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B-A22B’s MoE routing overhead will spike EXCAVA’s latency at scale—its 22B experts demand per-token gating that DeepSeek-R1-671B avoids with dense layers. Swap to DeepSeek-R1-671B for now; benchmark both on EXCAVA’s live traffic—if Qwen3’s throughput drops >0.5% or costs rise >1%, revert.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt DeepSeek-R1-671B as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its dense 671B parameters deliver consistent latency without MoE’s routing overhead, which matters more than raw benchmark speed for our live traffic. The trade-off is higher per-token cost, but we mitigate it by running on Cerebras CS-3—its wafer-scale hardware cuts compute time enough to offset the price jump. Benchmark against Qwen3-235B-A22B immediately; if latency stays flat and costs rise under 1%, we lock it in.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-R1-671B’s per-token cost on Cerebras CS-3 will drown EXCAVA in bills before latency gains matter—Cerebras’ pricing scales with compute time, not output tokens, and 671B dense layers burn cycles. Benchmark Qwen3-235B-A22B on Cerebras’ MoE-optimized stack first; if its 0.5% throughput loss is acceptable, adopt it—otherwise default to a smaller dense model like Llama-4-17B for cost control.
